newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Apr 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Apr 11.

text.p: THE DOMINION

Sturt told to take break from SFO: Serious Fraud Office director Chas Sturt has stood down from his job for an unspecified period due to ill health, after being asked to do so by the State Services Commissioner. Page 1.

Compulsory super scheme 'could lead to less saving': Government-appointed Retirement Commissioner Colin Blair says a compulsory superannuation scheme could mean New Zealanders saved less, not more. Page 2.

Convicted Tam retains job with Youth Affairs Ministry: Convicted wife-beater and former Mongrel Mob gang mamber Harry Tam is to keep his job as a policy analyst with the Youth Affairs Ministry. Page 2.
Peters hints at building rethink: The decision to build a $94 million ministerial wing at Parliament might be reviewed during the Budget round. Page 2.

Treasury defends itself over ridiculed report: The Treasury has defended itself against the ridicule aimed at one of its reports that said employing more police would cause more justice system costs because they would catch more criminals. Page 2.

Defence pact still valuable, says East: The Five Power Defence Arrangement was still important to New Zealand, Defence Minister Paul East said on Thursday. East leaves for Singapore and Malaysia on Friday for a triennial meeting of arrangement ministers. Page 2.

Leap in Warehouse shares brings caution: The Warehouse Group share price soared 16 percent after the company posted robust profit growth on Wednesday, but other retailers are wary of declaring the beginning of a retail recovery. Page 11.

Garlick staff go in restructuring move: Wellington brokerage Garlick and Co has cut staff numbers in what it described as a forerunner to an "enormous restructuring" for the broking industry. Page 11.
Sharp fall in consumer confidence detected: Consumer confidence fell sharply in the March quarter, according to a WestpacTrust McDermott Miller survey. Page 11.
Progressive moving to two chains: Progressive Enterprises planned to realign its business into two supermarket chains from the present three, chief executive Graeme Kelly said on Thursday. Page 11.

Profits doubled by Citibank NZ: Citibank's New Zealand operations more than doubled its after-tax profit to $8.02 million for the year to December 31. The $3.46 million profit reported a year earlier was affected by a $4.40 million loss in other revenues. Page 11.

Tranzrich gets approval to buy bus franchise: Masterton's Tranzrich Travel has been given Commerce Commission clearance to buy the InterCity bus franchise and assets of Guthreys InterCity Coach Services. Page 11.
Force Corp to raise $18.75m: Cinema operator Force Corporation plans to raise $18.75 million through a share placement to pay for its expansion in Argentina. Page 11.

Westfield takes St Lukes management: Australian shopping mall owner and manager Wastfield Holdings would manage St Lukes Group's New Zealand shopping centres from May 1, St Lukes said on Thursday. Page 11.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD

Cabinet split on $94m 'palace': The coalition cabinet is split over whether to cancel construction of the controversial $94 million ministerial wing behind the Beehive as pressure mounts for a rethink.

Fraud office reopens inquiry into BNZ: The Serious Fraud Office -- under a temporary director -- has reopened inquiries into the Bank of New Zealand's dealings after maintaining for several years that there was no need for a formal investigation.

CBD plans $40m property float: Commercial property company CBD New Zealand is seeking to raise around $40 million through a sharemarket float. A prospectus is expected to be registered later this month for a listing around May, according to narket sources.
Saatchi grabs talent: Auckland advertising agency M&C Saatchi is claiming a major coup after convincing one of the world's best-known creative teams to join its staff.

Australian listing gives Trans Tasman Properties flexibility: The float of Trans Tasman Properties' Australian assets would enable the company to turn from a position that forces it to lose out on a rising market, executive director Chris Canning said on Thursday.
New retirement ad ready: A North Shore couple, Jim and Mildred Collins and their family are the focus of a new advertising campaign by the retirement commissioner, which begins on Sunday.

HK company buys Symonds Street land: Hong Kong company Surelight Development Ltd has bought the 4ha of land on Symonds Street which the Auckland City Council acquired in a swap with Brierley Investments three years ago.

Contracting of elderly care likely to grow: The trend towards Regional Health Authorities contracting out nursing home and hospital health care for the elderly will accelerate over the next few years, according to Peter Fitzsimmons, chairman of Metropolitan Lifecare Group.
